D precedes E (cover with clean dry sheet / prevent hypothermia) because covering a still-contaminated or unrinsed torso would trap the agent and defer irrigation. F (reassess skin/pain/temperature/neurovascular) is terminal.

Under American Red Cross / ERC combined pediatric protocol: A → B → C → D. D is terminal under both because it is contingent on loss of responsiveness.
